Article Title: ED detects Rs 60 crore ‘irregularities’ after 24-hour search at TMC MP Nadimul Haque’s premises
Article Text:
TMC MP Nadimul Haque was in Ranchi in neighbouring Jharkhand when the operation began (File photo)

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) concluded searches at the premises of Trinamool Congress (TMC) Rajya Sabha MP Nadimul Haque early Tuesday morning, bringing an end to a marathon search operation that lasted more than 24 hours.According to officials, the central agency detected financial irregularities amounting to around Rs 60 crore in an Urdu newspaper linked to Haque.“Financial records and digital documents are being examined to establish the trail of the transactions and determine the nature and source of the funds under investigation,” an ED official told PTI on condition of anonymity.The probe agency is investigating alleged illegal financial transactions involving the newspaper and examining whether some funds were routed through hawala channels.During the searches, the ED examined bank records, financial documents and digital material, and questioned Haque at his residence and office in Kolkata.Investigators are also looking into the alleged movement of funds linked to the TMC.According to ED sources, investigators found discrepancies in transactions worth around Rs 60 crore and could not immediately find satisfactory supporting records. The agency is examining whether the transactions were genuine business dealings or whether the funds were moved through informal channels, including hawala.Similar searches were conducted at seven other locations in Delhi and Ranchi, including the newspaper’s office in Kolkata's Park Circus and premises linked to Haque.The TMC MP was in Ranchi in neighbouring Jharkhand when the operation began and was subsequently brought to Kolkata on Monday night, where he was questioned during searches at his residence and office.The investigation stems from an FIR registered by the Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate and a subsequent Enforcement Case Information Report filed by the ED. The case involves allegations of illegal and unaccounted financial transactions and receipt of funds from suspicious sources.The ED has not made any arrests in the case so far.
Article Summary: TMC MP Nadimul Haque was in Ranchi in neighbouring Jharkhand when the operation began. He was subsequently brought to Kolkata on Monday night, where he was questioned. The case involves allegations of illegal and unaccounted financial transactions and receipt of funds from suspicious sources.

Article Title: 'Some can never be happy with India's progress': PM Modi renews 'naraz fufa' jibe at Congress in Vadodara
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated development projects worth over thirty-five thousand crore rupees in Vadodara. He highlighted the successful completion of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor sections connecting key industrial hubs. The Prime Minister also criticised previous governments for significant delays in executing the freight corridor project and emphasised the transformation in the nation's work culture and logistics system since 2014.

Where will the trucks go?

'How country's work culture has transformed?'

Event draws huge response

Rs 35,000 crore projects launched

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday renewed his "naraz fufa" jibe at the Congress, saying "some people could never be happy with India's progress."The Prime Minister received an enthusiastic welcome at the ‘NaMo for Viksit Bharat’ event, with organisers saying all seats were booked within an hour of online ticket sales opening.The programme featured music and cultural performances, including a rendition of Queen’s ‘We Will Rock You’, as the crowd cheered for the PM.Addressing the ‘NaMo for Viksit Bharat’ event in Vadodara, PM Modi said a recent double-stack container freight train from Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT) in Mumbai to Vadodara carried cargo equivalent to more than 250 trucks in a single trip."Recently, a double-stack container freight train was operated from JNPT (Mumbai) to Vadodara—meaning the train ran with one container stacked on top of another," he said."With this single trip, the volume of cargo transported from Mumbai to Vadodara was equivalent to that of over 250 trucks. Now, enter the 'naraaz fufa' figure—the one who will immediately start complaining: "What about the truck drivers? Where will the trucks go? What will happen to those who bought trucks?" Well, 'fufa' has found something to grumble about now..." he added.PM Modi said the freight corridor would reduce travel time and logistics costs while saving fuel and benefiting the environment.“Today, the work on the 2,800-kilometer corridor has been successfully completed. The Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors are now becoming the backbone of the nation's trade and commerce,” he said.The Prime Minister also credited his government with speeding up the freight corridor project after 2014, while criticising the previous government for delays."In 2014, the people of Vadodara, Gujarat, and the entire nation sent me from Gujarat to Delhi. The previous government remained in power until 2014; you sent me there, and they were shown the door. In 7-8 years, not even a single kilometer of work on the freight corridor had been completed. Had the country been run according to their methods, who knows—even three or four subsequent generations might have passed without it ever getting done. That was the state in which they had left a project meant to transform India's logistics ecosystem. After 2014, I set about accelerating this work immediately."The Prime Minister said the project had transformed the country's logistics system and reflected a change in work culture."This Dedicated Freight Corridor stands as a testament to how the country's work culture has transformed over the last 12 years. The concept for this Dedicated Freight Corridor was first mooted in 2004... A special company was formed in 2006 to execute this project. Yet, until 2014, the files merely shuttled back and forth; they were just traveling from one table to another. And look at the irony—even these files did not get the benefit of a dedicated corridor. .." he added.The ‘NaMo for Viksit Bharat Vadodara’ programme was organised as part of PM Modi's visit to the city, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for various development projects.Gujarat deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi said the programme had received an overwhelming response from residents. For the first time, online ticketing was introduced, with all available seats booked within 60 minutes. Demand was reportedly three times higher than the available capacity.Special fan zones were also set up to accommodate people who could not get seats inside the venue.Ahead of PM Modi’s visit, a ‘Viksit Bharat Padayatra’ was organised on Monday under Sanghavi’s leadership. The march began at the Faculty of Technology in Dandia Bazaar and passed through Kirti Stambh before concluding at Sursagar Lake.A cultural programme was also organised at Sursagar Lake, featuring singer Kailash Kher. ‘Swachhata Doots’ who contributed to keeping Vadodara clean were felicitated during the event.During his visit, Modi inaugurated, dedicated and laid the foundation stones for development projects worth more than Rs 35,000 crore in Vadodara.A major highlight was the inauguration of three sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC), covering 326 route kilometres and developed at a cost of more than Rs 20,700 crore.The sections connect New Sanand (North) with New Makarpura, New Umbergaon with New Saphale, and New Saphale with New JNPT in Mumbai. The connectivity to Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority is expected to speed up the movement of export-import cargo, improve links between industrial centres and ports and reduce logistics costs.PM Modi also flagged off freight train services from the newly connected sections and a new passenger train between Tanda Road and Vadodara’s Pratapnagar.He dedicated the Jobat-Tanda Road new rail line to the nation. The line, developed as part of the Chhota Udepur-Dhar project, will connect remote and tribal areas of Alirajpur with the national railway network.The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for three railway projects covering 329 km at a cost of more than Rs 9,700 crore, along with three National Highway projects worth around Rs 1,780 crore.Several Gujarat government projects worth around Rs 2,600 crore were also inaugurated or launched, including housing projects under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, a water-supply project for 11 villages in eastern Vadodara, the Vadodara Urban Development Authority Ring Road Phase II and a 110 MW floating solar project at Kadana Dam.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi inaugurated development projects worth over thirty-five thousand crore rupees in Vadodara. He highlighted the successful completion of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor sections connecting key industrial hubs. The Prime Minister also criticised previous governments for significant delays in executing the freight corridor project.

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane expressed support for the Vishva Hindu Parishad 's (VHP) call to bar Muslims from the Navratri events in the state, alleging that otherwise this would lead to an increase in "love jihad" cases.Attendees at such festivities should undergo identity checks and recite the Hanuman Chalisa before entry, the BJP leader told PTI Videos on Monday."Love jihad" is a term used by right-wing activists to allege a ploy by Muslim men to lure women (mostly from the Hindu community) into relationships for religious conversion."Those who do not follow idol worship should not participate in Hindu religious events. Those coming for garba should show their identity and chant the Hanuman Chalisa before being allowed entry," Rane said, extending support to the VHP's demand.The VHP last week announced that Muslims "would not be allowed" entry to garba and dandiya venues across the state during the upcoming Navratri festival, and issued "guidelines" for organisers to verify participants' identities by checking their Aadhaar cards and applying tilak on their foreheads.The Navratri festival will begin on October 11.On the demand to curb DJ sound systems during the upcoming Ganesh festival, Rane called for the rules to be applied uniformly to all religious processions.“If DJs are not permitted during Ganesh festival celebrations, similar restrictions should apply to Eid processions as well,” he said.Rane alleged that loud music was played late into the night during recent Eid processions, adding that Hindus follow court orders and noise regulations.He also slammed Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray over his reported remarks about alleged vulgar dances during Kanwar Yatra events in parts of Uttar Pradesh, questioning why criticism was directed only at Hindu practices while statements by Muslim clerics were not similarly discussed.The BJP minister asserted that some people were attempting to "defame" Hinduism and Sanatan Dharma.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday condemned the death of Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh, who was allegedly assaulted by a group of men in Delhi.In a social media post on X, Rahul questioned Union home minister Amit Shah and Delhi Police over what they were doing to stop the growing lawlessness against people from the Northeast in Delhi."Chongtham Vikram Singh ji, a renowned musician from Manipur, went downstairs to ask some men to lower the noise outside his home. He was beaten to death for it. A father, killed outside his own home, in his own country's capital. After many such incidents, every Northeast family in Delhi is asking the same question today - are we safe here?" the Congress leader said."What are Shah's MHA and Delhi Police doing to stop this growing lawlessness, especially against people from the Northeast? There must be a swift investigation, and the culprits must be brought to justice. My condolences to Vikram ji's family," he added.The 54-year-old Manipuri music teacher allegedly died after being assaulted by a group of men in Kilokari Village, in Delhi’s Ashram area, following a dispute over noise and nuisance outside his residence.According to police, Vikram Singh had objected to alleged shouting and nuisance by delivery boys and dhaba staff opposite his house. When he came downstairs to object, he was allegedly attacked with fists and blows.Vikram was taken to Holy Family Hospital by his son Yaiphaba for treatment, where he later succumbed to his injuries.According to the Police, a PCR call regarding the alleged beating of C Vikram Singh was received at Delhi's Sunlight Colony police station on September 7. Police said the preliminary enquiry indicated that Singh had objected to alleged shouting and nuisance by delivery boys and dhaba staff in front of his residence in Kilokari Village. When he came downstairs and objected, he was allegedly assaulted with fists and blows.The official further informed that they have registered an FIR under murder provisions and said all the accused, including minors, have been apprehended.Further investigation is still under way.

DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday following intense protests demanding the expunging of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks regarding former Chief Minister M Karunanidhi, late Union Minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission, and ED dossiers in recent cases.The situation turned chaotic after Speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge the remarks, ruling that Vijay had merely cited the Sarkaria Commission, which had been discussed at length in the House previously. Declaring that there was no need to expunge the remarks, the Speaker gave his ruling, triggering further escalation as DMK members upped the ante, raised slogans, and brought the proceedings to a standstill by sitting in the well of the House.The Speaker urged the protesting members to return to their seats, offering to allow DMK whip E V Velu and deputy leader of the opposition K N Nehru to speak on the issue. He also cautioned Kallakurichi MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan against approaching the chair.Marshals subsequently entered the House and physically removed the protesting MLAs, carrying out members including Kutty (Valparai), Durai Chandrasekaran (Thiruvaiyaru), Vasantham Karthikeyan (Rishivandiyam) and a few more who refused to budge from the well. The disruption halted assembly proceedings around 10:03 am, following earlier heated exchanges between former ministers Velu and Nehru and ministers Aadhav Arjuna and R Nirmalkumar.
Article Summary: DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday following intense protests. They were demanding the expunging of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks regarding former Chief Minister M Karunanidhi, late Union Minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission, and ED dossiers in recent cases. Article Title: Delhi building collapse: SC appointed amicus curiae seeks safety audit of PGs, hostels across capital
Article Text:
6 killed in Satya Niketan building collapse; FIR against owner

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae on Wednesday filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan and requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities across Delhi.Senior advocate Ajit Kumar Sinha, in his report, said that the Satya Niketan incident assumes significance as the locality had witnessed another building collapse in April 2022, in which two people were killed and four injured.“The present incident is also required to be viewed in the context of an earlier building collapse in Satya Niketan in April 2022, in which two persons lost their lives, and four others were injured. The recurrence of such an incident in the same locality raises serious concerns regarding the effectiveness of the existing mechanism for inspection, identification of dangerous structures, and enforcement of building bye-laws”, the amicus report said.He also noted that construction-related work was being undertaken in or around the basement and that there were reports of waterlogging in the basement immediately before the latest collapse.The amicus has sought a time-bound inspection and safety audit of PGs, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments around colleges and universities across Delhi, including checks on sanctioned building plans, actual construction and number of floors, basement construction and alterations, land use, structural and fire safety, ingress and egress, and dangerous or ruinous conditions.This comes after seven people were killed when a building collapsed in Satya Niketan on Sunday.Meanwhile, Municipal Corporation of Delhi also directed its executive engineers (building) across all zones to inspect structures under their jurisdiction and submit comprehensive reports by September 10, following the deadly building collapse in south Delhi's Satya Niketan, which killed seven people, officials said.Officials said the information collected during the inspections would be incorporated into an affidavit to be filed before the Delhi High Court within 10 days.The inspections and submission of reports will be personally monitored and supervised by the additional commissioners concerned in each zone, according to the order, they added.
Article Summary: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan. He requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities.

Article Title: AIIMS Delhi displays live population count of India: How does it get data on newly born babies?
Article Text:
AIIMS population display (Instagram)

A population clock, not a birth register

So why the number keeps changing

India's last completed population Census

​A population clock (Instagram)

What about babies born at AIIMS?

Why does the clock look so precise?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A digital clock is going viral in Delhi. Well, it’s not an ordinary clock. It’s a population counter clock which is displayed at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS Delhi). It has recently attracted attention online, with the number on the screen changing continuously and appearing to show India’s population growing every second. Now, this viral display has also raised an important question: if the number increases every few seconds, is AIIMS actually receiving information every time a baby is born somewhere in India?So the answer is NO.It’s a population clock and it is an estimate based on demographic data and population projections. It’s not a nationwide live birth-tracking system. The distinction is important because India does have official systems for recording births and deaths. These systems do not work like a real-time national counter.The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s National Health Profile identifies the Census, registration of vital events, population surveys, population projections and the Sample Registration System (SRS) among the sources used for demographic information.The Civil Registration System (CRS), maintained through the registration machinery of the government, is responsible for the continuous recording of vital events such as births and deaths. The Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner describes civil registration as the continuous, permanent and compulsory recording of the occurrence and characteristics of vital events.But this does not mean that a national population display receives an electronic notification every time a birth takes place in India.Now this is where population estimation comes in. A population clock takes a known or estimated population at a particular reference point and applies demographic rates to project how that population changes over time.If the estimated population is expected to rise by a certain number over a year, the annual change can be mathematically distributed across months, days, hours, minutes and seconds. A digital display can therefore make the number appear to be changing in real time.If the display increases by one, it does not necessarily mean that a particular baby has just been born somewhere in India. It represents a calculated movement in the estimated population total.India's last completed population Census was conducted in 2011, when the country's population was recorded at about 121.1 crore. The National Health Profile notes that India's population was projected to increase from 121.1 crore in 2011 to 152.2 crore by 2036, an increase of about 25% over 25 years.The United Nations follows a similar demographic approach. Its World Population Prospects 2024 provides population estimates and projections based on analyses of historical demographic trends for countries and territories around the world.The fact that the clock is located at AIIMS can easily create another misconception that AIIMS might somehow be using its maternity records to calculate India's population.Instead, births are recorded through the country's civil registration framework, while demographic agencies use registration data, surveys and statistical methods to understand population trends.That is perhaps the most fascinating part of the viral display.A computer can calculate an estimated population to several decimal places and refresh the display every second. That does not mean demographers know the exact number of people alive in India at that precise second.The changing digits are essentially a visualisation of a statistical model. It is similar to a countdown or a continuously updated financial index: the display can change every second even though the underlying information is based on data collected over a longer period.The viral AIIMS population clock is therefore best understood as a demographic awareness tool, not as a nationwide surveillance mechanism for births.India's population is certainly changing continuously. Babies are being born, people are dying and migration changes the distribution of people across regions. So, the next time the AIIMS population clock ticks upward, it does not mean that a computer has just received the birth certificate of another Indian baby.
Article Summary: A digital clock is going viral in Delhi. It’s a population counter clock which is displayed at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS Delhi) It has recently attracted attention online, with the number on the screen changing continuously. It has also raised an important question: is AIIMS actually receiving information every time a baby is born somewhere in India?

NEW DELHI: Taking note of another instance of a Shiv Sena politician in Maharashtra assaulting doctors, Supreme Court Monday said the situation in the state had worsened and favoured strict action against politicians to send a message that such behaviour against a medical practitioner would not be tolerated.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said people indulging in violence against doctors should be arrested without any delay. "They do not deserve to roam around," the bench said while referring to the recent incident of Sena workers assaulting doctors and hospital staff in Palghar.SC made the observations while hearing the plea of Sena corporator Ramesh Sukrya Mhatre, who is accused of assaulting doctors at Dombivli in July. He had moved SC against stringent conditions imposed by HC on him while granting bail last month. Sensing the mood of the court, senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi sought to withdraw the petition.The court allowed his plea for the withdrawal but before that, it expressed its concern over the growing number of incidents of doctors being attacked by politicians and said that it cannot be justified.Rohatgi said the group of people responsible for the assault in Palghar was different, but SC said they belonged to the same party. "Same ideology. How can this be justified that you go and assault them inside their chambers and beat them brutally? It's an issue of law and public order," the bench said. Mhatre was arrested in July for allegedly assaulting doctors and staff at a civic-run hospital in Dombivli on July 6.
Article Summary: Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said people indulging in violence against doctors should be arrested without any delay. "They do not deserve to roam around," the bench said while referring to the recent incident of Sena workers assaulting doctors and hospital staff in Palghar.

Article Title: Janmashtami lights up Antilia: Inside the Ambani family's Janmashtami celebration
Article Text: Antilia came alive with colour, devotion and festive cheer this week as the Ambani family celebrated Janmashtami, marking the birth of Lord Krishna.Footage from the evening shows the family's signature blend of devotion, colour and festive joy, a celebration that, over the years, has become one of the most talked-about traditions in India's festival calendar.The evening carried all the markers of a Janmashtami night. Flower-laden interiors dripping with strings of white and pink blooms, a dance floor painted with intricate motifs, and family members dressed in richly embroidered traditional silhouettes, deep purples, sea-greens, and reds threaded with gold. Prayers were offered with folded hands and floral garlands, following the rituals associated with the festival, which commemorates Krishna's birth at midnight and is celebrated across India and among Hindu communities worldwide with fasting, devotional singing, and the reenactment of Krishna's childhood.What stood out most in the visuals was the warmth, the women in the family twirling with children on the dance floor, a toddler being lifted into a gentle embrace mid-celebration, and quieter moments of prayer tucked between the festivities. It was a reminder that behind the headlines about India's best-known business family lies a fairly universal scene of generations coming together, in their finest clothes, to mark a day that matters to them.At its heart, though, the footage captures a family pausing from their famously packed schedules to celebrate a shared faith together, surrounded by children, colour, and candlelight. For a country as religiously and culturally diverse as India, it's worth remembering that such festival scenes, however grand the setting, echo similar celebrations happening in millions of homes on the same night, where the essentials remain unchanged: prayer, family, sweets, and a bit of dancing until midnight.
Article Summary: Antilia came alive with colour, devotion and festive cheer this week. The Ambani family celebrated Janmashtami, marking the birth of Lord Krishna. Footage from the evening shows the family's signature blend of devotion, colour and festive joy.

Article Title: Freight corridors to be finally operational fully after 2 decades
Article Text:
Dedicated Freight Corridor to become fully operational as PM Modi set to inaugurate final three sections of Western DFC, linking JNPT Port to Dadri. (Representative Image)

NEW DELHI: Nearly 20 years after the Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) project was approved, India’s freight rail network linking eastern, northern and western regions will become fully operational Tuesday, when PM Narendra Modi inaugurates three remaining sections of Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) today.WDFC connects Jawaharlal Nehru Port in Mumbai with Dadri in UP, where it intersects with Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC), completing the country’s dedicated freight rail backbone.On the eastern side, the DFC from Sonnangar in West Bengal to Ludhiana in Punjab is fully operational. Though EDFC was originally planned from Dankuni in West Bengal, a 538-km section from Dankuni to Sonnagar was de-scoped from the DFC project and multi-tracking of this part is now being carried out by railways.After its inauguration, the 2,843 km of WDFC and EDFC will become operational.In a statement, PMO said three sections — New Sanand-New Makarpura, New Umbergaon-New Saphale and New Saphale-New JNPT sections — that Modi will dedicate to the nation covers 326 route km and has been built with a more than Rs 20,700 crore investment.Direct connectivity of Jawahar Lal Nehru Port will facilitate faster movement of export-import cargo, strengthen connectivity between industrial centres and ports, reduce logistics costs and help decongest Mumbai’s railway network, it said.Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that before 2014, no physical work had been completed on the project. NDA govt took this forward by addressing long-pending challenges and resolving issues across different sections.According to railways, as of Aug, the already operational DFC stretches had handled approximately 5.2 lakh freight train trips, averaging around 435 trains per day. The dedicated freight network has generated around 658 billion gross tonne km (GTKM) and 360 billion net tonne km (NTKM).
Article Summary: Final three sections of Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) to be inaugurated today. WDFC connects Jawaharlal Nehru Port in Mumbai with Dadri in UP. It completes the country’s dedicated freight rail backbone.

Article Title: The annual Delhi Yamuna flood threat- why September matters?
Article Text:
2025: People, animals living near floodplains relocated on roads ( on left); Yamuna Flood plain board (on right) (Pic credit: Priyanka Jaiswal)

2025: When the Yamuna broke its banks

The warning numbers you should know

2026: Is Delhi facing another repeat?

2025 vs 2026 of Yamuna flood threat

The flood threat does not end with the water level

Know how a Yamuna flood unfolds in Delhi

Living with the Yamuna

Delhi Yamuna Floodplain (Pic credit: Priyanka Jaiswal)

Houses built around Delhi Yamuna Floodplain (Pic credit: Priyanka Jaiswal)

Animals: The overlooked victims

Buffaloes in the river | Fencing installed (Pic credit: Priyanka Jaiswal)

Delhi’s real test: Preparing before the next flood

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A year after the Yamuna inundated large parts of Delhi, the river is again flowing above the danger mark. The immediate threat may be lower this time, but heavy rain in the upper catchment could quickly change the picture, exposing how vulnerable the city’s floodplain still remains.That vulnerability is built into Delhi’s geography. Every monsoon, as September sets in, the city watches the Yamuna closely because even a sharp rise in the river or a sudden surge in upstream discharge can quickly put thousands living and working along the floodplains at risk.The danger mark at the Old Iron Railway Bridge is 205.33 metres, while evacuation of vulnerable residents begins when the river reaches around 206 metres. On September 6, the Yamuna was flowing at 205.59 metres, already slightly above the danger mark.And it is not just the people living along the river who feel the impact. When the Yamuna rises sharply, critical roads and infrastructure can also be affected. The Loha Pul, a vital link between Central Delhi (including Kashmere Gate and Old Delhi Railway Station) and East Delhi, is among the key crossings vulnerable to rising waters during severe floods.Last year, the warning turned into a full-blown crisis.The Yamuna crossed the danger mark and rose above 207 metres, inundating several low-lying parts of the Capital and forcing more than 10,000 people to evacuate vulnerable areas.The impact extended well beyond flooded homes. Roads and public infrastructure were affected, electricity supplies were disrupted and houses were left covered in mud and silt after the water receded. Thousands whose livelihoods depended on the floodplain also took a hit.Floodwaters reached the Ring Road and Outer Ring Road, disrupting traffic between Majnu ka Tilla and the Salimgarh bypass. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi stopped cremations at Nigambodh Ghat and the Geeta Colony ground because of flooding. Water-treatment infrastructure was also affected.A major factor was the enormous volume of water released from the Hathnikund Barrage in Haryana after intense rainfall in the upper Yamuna catchment.A year later, attention is once again turning to the Yamuna.The monsoon remains active, with heavy rain reported in parts of Delhi and northern India. The immediate concern is not simply the river’s current level, but how much water is being released upstream and whether intense rainfall in the catchment pushes those levels sharply higher.The Yamuna has remained comparatively stable this year, despite crossing the danger mark.Dr Shiv Singh Rawat, water expert and convener of the WalkForYamuna Campaign, said the difference becomes clearer when the upstream discharge is examined. “This year’s situation needs to be understood in its proper hydrological context. The maximum discharge released from Hathnikund Barrage during this year was around 64,000 cusecs, which is significantly below an extreme flood situation. That helps explain why Delhi experienced a much less severe river-flood situation than in 2025. ”But that relative stability offers no guarantee.The India Meteorological Department has warned of isolated heavy rainfall over Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi from September 10-12.Fairly widespread rain, accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning, is also likely over Uttarakhand from September 6-12, while rainfall disturbances are expected over Himachal Pradesh.For Delhi, what happens upstream can matter as much as what happens within the Capital itself.A spell of intense rainfall in the upper catchment can send a surge downstream, leaving communities along the floodplain with limited time to respond.The relatively stable Yamuna this year may have given Delhi a temporary reprieve, but the underlying vulnerability remains.The floodplain is not simply vacant land beside the river.It acts as a natural buffer during floods, helps recharge groundwater and performs an important ecological function.“The 2-km-stretch on both sides of Yamuna acts as a buffer for floods, restores groundwater balance and acts as an organic filter. However, excess rain will create flooding in Delhi, and sanitation is not adequate to handle floods in the Capital,” says environmentalist Kavita Ashok.Rawat warns that the greater danger could emerge gradually through construction and development. “The concern is that areas outside the most restrictive floodplain zones could gradually become corridors for permanent construction, infrastructure and commercial riverfront activity,” he says. “That would undermine the very floodplain functions that protect the city.”The question, therefore, is not only whether the Yamuna will rise this September. It is whether Delhi is becoming more or less vulnerable when it does.For families living along Delhi’s floodplain, the monsoon is not simply a season of heavy rain. It is a recurring threat of displacement.When the river rises, families may have to move their belongings, livestock and essentials to higher ground with little warning.The granddaughter of Ramu Sahni, who lives with his family near the Yamuna floodplain, told TOI that residents don’t receive any advance warning.“We receive no warning on time. We see the rise in the water level of Yamuna and ourselves decide to shift to the roads with all our belongings. The authorities then notice the crowd on the roads and help us with tents.”Sahni, who came to Delhi from Bihar in search of employment many years ago, says the relief arrangements have also changed. “Earlier, they used to provide us with some ration and water in tents but now the situation has changed,” he says. “I don’t live here for free, I pay rent.”For many residents, simply relocating permanently is not an easy option.Their lives are tied to the floodplain through work, transport, markets and social networks. When the water recedes, they return.“We return back here when the water recedes after 2 months. This is all we have. I run a rickshaw, we are mostly ragpickers. Where will we go?”That cycle of evacuation, waiting, returning and rebuilding has become part of life for many families.For families with livestock, evacuation is even more complicated.Leaving home is one thing. Moving buffaloes, cattle, calves and other animals to safety is another. Stray animals are even more vulnerable, particularly when rising water cuts off their escape routes.Sahni says livestock is not simply property for floodplain families, it is their livelihood. “People usually take their buffaloes with them on the roads. How will they earn? Now they have installed fencing around a small Yamuna pond here. How will buffaloes go there? They need to be there for survival. If a flood comes right now, there is no way we can rescue them immediately as there is only a small route to travel.”When asked who rescues stray animals during floods, he had no clear answer.PETA India told TOI that animals stranded during floods can face exhaustion, dehydration, hunger, injury and drowning, making rapid rescue and access to food, clean water and veterinary care critical.“The biggest challenge when trying to reach animals in emergency situations is getting to them in the first place. Access may be cut off by rising water, for instance,” said Sachin Bangera of PETA India.During last year’s floods, PETA India’s Rapid Response Team arranged a boat to rescue dogs stranded in flooded areas and at risk of drowning.“Animals who are left chained are the most vulnerable because they cannot escape, or they become exhausted and drown,” Bangera said.Aditi Bakshi, Animal Welfare Advocate and Specialist - Government and Public Policy at Mercy For Animals, says the problem goes deeper than rescue.“Many people are forced into an impossible choice by a system that gives them no option. Rescue boats and relief camps do not take animals. When the administration tells a family to evacuate and will not let them bring their cow, their pigs, or their two goats, the family has to choose between their children’s safety and the animal’s life.”She argues that flood preparedness must explicitly include animals.According to Bakshi, Delhi lacks a comprehensive operational framework covering animal evacuation, including a nodal officer, mapped animal shelters, pre-monsoon fodder stocks, evacuation protocols for large animals and regular drills. “A plan that has never been drilled is not a plan; it is a document,” she says.For Delhi’s floodplain residents, the Yamuna may rise for only a few days. The disruption can last months.That makes flood preparedness about far more than issuing warnings once the river begins to rise.“Relief must be immediate, but rehabilitation must be humane and sustainable. People should not have to repeatedly rebuild their lives every monsoon,” says Dr Heera Lal Patel, IAS.During a flood emergency, he says, authorities need to provide clear information, accessible evacuation routes, transport and safe shelters. Vulnerable families cannot be expected to organise an evacuation on their own.Rawat argues that Delhi needs scientifically determined, risk-based floodplain zoning.“The real measures of success are: how many people are taken out of high-risk locations, flood-storage capacity restored and new encroachment prevented.”For companion-animal guardians, PETA India recommends identifying safe locations where pets will be accepted, keeping an emergency kit ready, and ensuring animals are microchipped or wear collars with updated contact details.But the larger challenge is institutional.The Yamuna’s rise is predictable. The exact scale and timing of a flood may not be.For communities living beside the river, that distinction can mean the difference between having time to evacuate and scrambling for safety as the water arrives.And every September, Delhi faces the same question: when the Yamuna rises again, will the city be better prepared, or will thousands once again be forced to leave their lives behind?
Article Summary: A year after the Yamuna inundated large parts of Delhi, the river is again flowing above the danger mark. The immediate threat may be lower this time, but heavy rain in the upper catchment could quickly change the picture. The danger mark at the Old Iron Railway Bridge is 205.33 metres.

Article Title: IIT Mandi orders inquiry after poster says Shudras should ‘serve higher classes’
Article Text:
Controversial caste poster at IIT Mandi sparks row, institute orders inquiry into display

What the controversial poster said

Behera's Gita and ISKCON links

NEW DELHI: IIT Mandi has set up an inquiry after a Bhagavad Gita-themed poster displayed on its campus during Janmashtami celebrations described Shudras as being meant to "serve higher classes", triggering controversy over caste discrimination.Institute Director Laxmidhar Behera said the poster was part of a student-led event and had not been approved by the institute. He said he was "shocked" when he learnt about the display and stressed that IIT Mandi does not support caste-based discrimination.In an email to the IIT Mandi community on Sunday, Behera described the development as an "Outright condemnation of recent poster display within campus". He said the poster, displayed on September 4, had not been endorsed by the institute "in any manner"."I have personally fought against caste-based discrimination in any form in every forum. I have instituted an enquiry committee in this matter such that the institute campus is never used for any such violation of social harmony. I fully empathise with members of our community who have been hurt by this incident," he wrote.Behera said IIT Mandi was committed to "the values of equality, social justice, scientific temper" and the principles laid down in the Constitution."The institute strongly condemns any form of caste based discrimination," he said, urging members of the campus community to "stand together against such biases/discrimination in any form".Speaking to PTI, Behera said the poster had been prepared for a student event. He said the inquiry committee included faculty members and representatives from different social categories, including members of the Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes.The poster, titled "Bhagavad Gita - The Timeless Wisdom", was put up outside the institute's auditorium during Janmashtami celebrations.It divided society into four groups mentioned in the Bhagavad Gita, namely Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. It described Brahmanas as those who "spread God's message", Kshatriyas as those who "protect society and spirituality" and Vaishyas as those who "drive economy, support others".For Shudras, however, the poster listed their role as "serve higher classes", which became the focus of the controversy.The poster also quoted a Bhagavad Gita verse stating that the four divisions of human society were created according to the "three modes of material nature and the work associated with them".Behera said he had been away from IIT Mandi and returned on Saturday. He said he learnt about the controversy on Sunday morning."I have not seen the poster. I don't want to take a side here and let the panel decide," he told PTI.The controversy has also drawn attention to Behera's long association with the Bhagavad Gita and ISKCON.According to his official IIT Mandi profile, Behera has spent 27 years teaching what he describes as the "universal principles of peace through Bhagavad Gita". He is also known as "HG Lila Purushottam Das" and is the founder of the proposed Bhaktivedanta University, whose website describes it as an ISKCON initiative.Behera currently teaches a three-credit course on the Bhagavad Gita at IIT Mandi.He defended ISKCON's position on caste, saying the organisation opposes discrimination and promotes equality."ISKCON is the only organisation that strictly and strongly speaks against caste-based discrimination. In ISKCON, pujaris are also from the Shudra community. Muslims are also pujaris," he claimed."We are against casteism in all forms. All occupational duties are according to guna and karma," he added.Behera also highlighted what he said was increased representation of marginalised communities at IIT Mandi during his tenure. According to him, the institute had no OBC, SC or ST faculty members when he joined, while their numbers have since risen substantially. The IIT director has previously faced criticism over his public views.In 2023, he asked students to take a pledge against eating meat and linked landslides and cloudbursts in Himachal Pradesh to cruelty towards animals. In 2022, shortly after becoming IIT Mandi director, a video surfaced in which he claimed to have helped a friend's family get rid of "evil spirits" through chanting holy mantras.More recently, IIT Mandi's Indian Knowledge System and Mental Health Applications Centre held a conference in June that included sessions on the Bhagavad Gita, Ayurveda and reincarnation. Behera was among its general chairs and co-organised a session titled "Reincarnation, OBEs and afterlife communication".The institute's inquiry committee will now examine how the poster was prepared, displayed and presented during the student-led event.
Article Summary: IIT Mandi sets up inquiry after Bhagavad Gita-themed poster sparks controversy. Poster described Shudras as being meant to "serve higher classes" Institute Director Laxmidhar Behera said the poster was part of a student-led event. He said he was "shocked" when he learnt about the display and stressed that IITMandi does not support caste-based discrimination.

Article Title: Company can be punished for offence carrying imprisonment, term can be replaced by fine: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A company having no physical body cannot be imprisoned and having no mind cannot possess mens rea (guilty mind), which is essential for conviction in a criminal case. So can a firm be convicted and punished?SC Monday answered the tricky questions by holding that a company can be convicted even when it cannot have a guilty mind of its own and can also be punished, though the punishment of a jail term can be substituted by a fine.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Manoj Misra said there is a need to bring a law for corporate criminal liability but said the issue comes within the legislature's prerogative and it cannot be done by a court. It held that a company is not rendered immune to prosecution merely because the offence carries a mandatory sentence of imprisonment. Referring to a constitution bench ruling, the bench said a judicial discretion to impose a fine alone must be read into such provisions when dealing with juristic persons."The position under Indian law is thus clear that a corporation can be prosecuted for an offence notwithstanding that it carries a mandatory sentence of imprisonment or requires proof of mens rea. It appears that a corporation cannot be prosecuted only where the offence is punishable with imprisonment alone, or where the offence, by its nature, requires personal malicious intent, such that it is incapable of commission by a corporation at all," the bench said.SC passed the order on a plea by Sanofi India Ltd which said a prosecution against a corporation like it, for an offence requiring mens rea, is maintainable only where a natural person has been identified and arraigned as an accused alongside it. It said that corporations alone cannot be convicted and pleaded that proceedings against it should be quashed. Rejecting the plea of the company, the bench said non-identification of the natural person does not, by itself, render the allegations incapable of disclosing the corporation's role in the offence.The case pertains to the supply of pharmaceutical products by Sanofi India to Bhabha Atomic Research Centre. As per CBI, a BARC officer had conspired with the company to procure medicines at inflated prices and in quantities exceeding the requirement. A case was registered against Sanofi, which challenged its prosecution on the ground that none of its employees had been made accused and a company alone cannot be prosecuted."... where the surrounding facts and circumstances, taken as a whole, disclose the possibility that the corporation acted with the requisite mens rea, that disclosure is not defeated merely because no particular individual has been identified as its source. Therefore, the ingredient of mens rea can still be disclosed even where no individual has been identified," the bench said while rejecting the plea of the company.
Article Summary: Justices J B Pardiwala and Manoj Misra said there is a need to bring a law for corporate criminal liability. The issue comes within the legislature's prerogative and it cannot be done by a court. The case pertains to the supply of pharmaceutical products by Sanofi India.

NEW DELHI: CCTV footage has captured the moment a multi-storey building collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan area, killing six people and triggering a major rescue operation.The building, which housed a boys' paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus, collapsed around 1.30 pm on Sunday while repair and construction work was underway. The death toll rose to six after one more person rescued during the night was declared dead.The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped.Multiple agencies, including the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Service, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Delhi Disaster Management Authority, have been involved in the operation."One more person was rescued during the night but was brought dead, taking the toll to six," Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel said, PTI reported.Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has also been ordered. Officials are continuing efforts to trace people allegedly connected with the incident.To the residents, the collapse felt like a quake. “We felt the ground shake.When we ran outside, we saw that a house had completely collapsed,” said Roshan Pal, a student from Lucknow.“When I came out, a cloud of dust was spreading in all directions. That’s when we realised that the building had collapsed. We started removing one part of a wall soon after. Seven students were under it,” said Rahul Gaur, a resident, TOI reported.According to AIIMS, the JPN Apex Trauma Centre received 10 patients injured in the building collapse. Of the 10 patients, five were brought dead, while another patient who was in critical condition later succumbed to injuries.Three patients have been admitted and are undergoing treatment. One of them underwent limb surgery, while another patient with minor injuries was discharged after observation.Investigators are examining whether construction work carried out in the basement may have contributed to the collapse.Initial inquiries suggested that the basement was prone to waterlogging, which may have weakened the structure. Investigators are now examining whether construction work aggravated the situation and contributed to the collapse.The MCD is also looking into the matter. Similar concerns over basement work, water accumulation and the structural condition of the building have emerged in the preliminary probe.Police are likely to examine whether permission had been obtained for the work and why construction was being carried out during the monsoon, sources said. "The building owner, contractor and labourers will be interrogated," an investigator said, TOI reported.It was not immediately clear whether the building owner had obtained permission for the construction or whether the work was being carried out illegally, allegedly in connivance with local authorities.According to the MCD, the premises of Building/House No. 13, Satya Niketan, New Delhi, was found to be in a "ruinous, dangerous condition" and posed a threat to people occupying, visiting or passing by the building as well as those in the neighbourhood.Under Section 348 of the DMC Act, 1957, read with Section 491 of the Act, the MCD has ordered the property to be demolished within three days of receipt of the order.The order said that if the owner fails to comply within the specified period, the MCD will demolish the building and recover the demolition charges as arrears of tax.The collapse has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated areas of Delhi.Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations.“What is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?” Selja said.Former Delhi chief secretary Omesh Saigal said the incident should not be viewed in isolation and raised concerns over unauthorised construction in parts of the capital."Look at the kind of buildings constructed in Delhi—I would say that in some areas, one in five buildings is unauthorised; either the blueprints weren't approved, extra floors were added, or the construction is substandard," he said.Saigal also called for restrictions on new construction in areas that are already overcrowded. "At the very least, we should ban new construction in these areas. We must halt new construction or stop sanctioning building plans, for areas that are already over-congested and over-built. These are the things that need to be addressed," he added.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped. Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has been ordered.

Article Title: Strategic Autonomy in motion as India hosts 18th BRICS Summit
Article Text:
This would be the 18th summit of the grouping. (Photo: ANI)

India for BRICS

Key Challenges for India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India will host the annual BRICS summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, returning to the venue where it held the G20 summit in 2023. That gathering is remembered for the inclusion of the African Union in G20, marking a major step in efforts to bridge the gap between the Western-led global order and the emerging Global South. At BRICS, India will look to leverage that momentum, working with major emerging economies to demand structural reforms of global governance institutions dominated by the West.This would be the 18th summit of the grouping that brings together 11 major emerging and developing economies – Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Ethiopia, UAE, Indonesia, Iran, Egypt and Saudi Arabia – along with 10 other partner countries. Together, BRICS nations account for 49 percent of world population, 40 percent of global GDP and 26 percent of international trade.The last time India hosted an in-person BRICS summit was in 2016 in Goa. This year also marks 2 decades of formalisation of the bloc for cooperation on issues related to global economic and political governance. The theme of India's 2026 chairship is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability, drawing inspiration from PM Narendra Modi's 'humanity first' and people-centric approach to BRICS.This will also be the first summit to see in-person participation by Russian President Vladimir Putin since the start of the Ukraine war. Chinese President Xi Jinping is also visiting India for the first time in 7 years to participate in the summit.Under its chairship, India has so far held over 350 meetings - 25 at the ministerial level including the foreign ministers and national security advisers’ engagements. The ministerial meetings have so far resulted in key outcomes and initiatives spanning agriculture, health, energy, environment, disaster management and also trade, reaffirming commitment to a fair, inclusive and transparent multilateral trading system with WTO at its core.Despite the political fragmentation and economic imbalances associated with the grouping, BRICS remains important for India for multiple reasons, especially in an increasingly uncertain world. For one, it lends India a platform to practice its strategic autonomy and multi-alignment policy, not allowing any one single bloc to acquire excessive leverage over it. That it can simultaneously expand its strategic and technology ties with the West and also work with Quad for a free and open Indo-Pacific reinforces an independent foreign policy. For India, as external affairs minister S Jaishankar has said, BRICS is an embodiment of a multipolar world. India is not giving up on its Western partnerships, only hedging against uncertainty whether from US unpredictability or Chinese ascendancy.BRICS also allows India to showcase its Global South leadership credentials, as it works with other major emerging markets to push for reforms of global institutions like the UNSC, IMF and World Bank that are not representative of the developing world. Support for UNSC reforms is important, although it still falls short of an explicit endorsement of India's permanent membership bid, mainly because of China's presence.India's approach to BRICS is also guided by its complex ties with China. Turning away would mean allowing China to single-handedly shape the agenda of the developing world. BRICS is consensus driven and even for Washington and other Western capitals, India's moderating influence should be of significance as it prevents the bloc from turning into an anti-West platform.There's focus as well on expanding financial architecture as no government would like its trade to be held hostage by instruments it can't control. As Jaishankar has underlined, institutions such as the New Development Bank and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement demonstrate the group's ability to create credible alternatives. For India, these are not initiatives targeted at any currency. In any case, India has officially said it's against de-dollarisation or any attempt to target the US currency. It has also ruled out any proposal for a common BRICS currency.BRICS provides India with markets, along with trade diversification, de-risking and supply-chain opportunities. According to a commerce ministry press release, intra-BRICS merchandise trade reached approximately $1.17 trillion in 2024. India exported an estimated $82 billion in goods to BRICS members in FY2025–26, alongside approximately $31.3 billion in services exports in 2024. BRICS membership deepens India’s trade relationships with Russia (energy), Brazil (agriculture/commodities), Gulf and African countries, diversifying away from overreliance on any single partner.The first of course is to forge a consensus on West Asia that would enable a joint BRICS declaration, a task complicated by the presence of the UAE and Iran in the group. India would not like the event to end with a Chair's Statement, like what happened with the foreign ministers' meeting, knowing well that no BRICS summit has concluded without a comprehensive joint declaration. Foreign secretary Vikram Misri said last week India has received cooperation from all members and the government is working to arrive eventually at a constructive outcome that benefits all BRICS stakeholders. India will focus on drafting a resolution rooted in the UN Charter, dialogue and diplomacy, freedom of navigation and civilian protection, while looking to ringfence economic agreements from contentious political issues by acknowledging respective national positions.Balancing relations with the US is another key concern for India, which is hosting the summit fresh off a tariff firestorm with Washington. US President Donald Trump sees the grouping itself as an assault on the US currency and has threatened to impose 100 percent tariffs on BRICS nations if they work to replace the US dollar. India backs legitimate local-currency settlement, while maintaining it is against any common BRICS currency or China-centered replacement mechanism. As it walks the diplomatic tightrope, India must steer initiatives like the integration of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) but without appearing to endorse any anti-dollar bloc.Another challenge for India is to prevent China's predominance without destabilising its bilateral relations with Beijing. For all the talk about BRICS' combined power, China enjoys a vastly asymmetrical influence with its trade, investment, manufacturing and critical mineral leverage. Wary of China's efforts to advance its own economic interests, India has not endorsed SCO’s 2030 economic roadmap and it must find a way to work with China in BRICS on shared objectives but without allowing the forum to be co-opted as a Chinese economic or geopolitical platform.This also intersects with the challenge of ensuring that an expanded grouping remains governable and cohesive, especially with countries like Pakistan and Bangladesh pursuing membership with support from Beijing. True multipolarity and consensus-driven equality within the organisation are key imperatives for India.As Jaishankar said while announcing India's summit agenda, BRICS must transition now from a forum for discussions to a platform for delivery. In that spirit, India seems focused on delivering an outcome-oriented summit with key deliverables like a unanimous BRICS declaration, logistics supply-chain cooperation framework, incubator/ startup network, development finance, cross-border payment and continued support for Indian priorities like UNSC reforms and counterterrorism.The inclusion of the African Union was not the only major takeaway from the G20 summit in 2023. Perhaps more dramatic was the last-minute consensus on Ukraine through a compromise language crafted by India, allowing a G20 declaration. India can take confidence from that diplomatic triumph, heading into another tough but potentially rewarding global summit.
Article Summary: India will host the annual BRICS summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, returning to the venue where it held the G20 summit in 2023. This would be the 18th summit of the grouping that brings together 11 major emerging and developing economies – Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Ethiopia, UAE, Indonesia, Iran, Egypt and Saudi Arabia.

India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of UN General Assembly's Sept 4 resolution, "Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World's Regions, Particularly Africa".MEA said the resolution's purpose is to encourage the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses, and it neither adopts nor authenticates any particular world map, nor does it address political cartography, including international boundaries, disputed territories or place names."India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation, stressing the underlying principle of promoting equal-area cartographic representation. We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries," said Randhir Jaiswal.The resolution received abstentions from Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine, and a lone vote against it from US.The resolution noted that the Mercator projection remains widely used in educational, media, digital and official materials, despite the considerable distortion of landmasses to the North and South, far from the equator.It expressed concern that this distortion contributed to minimising the perceived sizes of Africa, Latin America and South Asia, and perpetuating an unbalanced view of the world. India welcomed the intention behind the resolution to promote more accurate and representative cartographic practices.
Article Summary: India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of UN General Assembly's Sept 4 resolution. Article Title: Passive smoking deaths up 50% since 1990: Lancet
Article Text:
Passive smoking deaths up 50% since 1990: Lancet

NEW DELHI: Deaths linked to second-hand smoke in India have soared, surging almost 50% since 1990 and claiming 325,600 lives in 2023 alone. According to a study published in The Lancet Public Health Monday, India had the world's second-highest number of people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, after China, with 444 million Indians affected.While India's age-standardised exposure prevalence declined from 43.2% to 30.6% over the last three decades, the absolute number of people exposed rose from 375 million in 1990 to 444 million in 2023, an increase of 18.4%. The health toll also rose sharply, with deaths attributable to second-hand smoke climbing from 217,700 to 325,600 during the same period.Fatalities among women rose from 113,400 to 156,900, while deaths among men from 104,300 to 168,700 over the same period. Second-hand smoke also accounted for 9.28 million disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in India in 2023, representing healthy years lost to premature death, illness or disability.Dr G C Khilnani, chairperson of pulmonary, critical care at PSRI Hospital, said, "Second-hand smoke contributes not only to illness and disability but also to premature deaths and loss of healthy years. Kids and women are particularly vulnerable, with children's developing lungs making them more susceptible to respiratory issues.Smoking should be done outdoors, and greater public awareness is needed."The study links second-hand smoke to ischaemic heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, breast cancer, type 2 diabetes, asthma and lower respiratory infections. Among children, lower respiratory infections were the leading contributor to the disease burden.Globally, 2.71 billion people were exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, contributing to 1.66 million deaths and 44.8 million DALYs. China, India and Indonesia accounted for nearly half of world's exposed population, with China recording 664 million exposed people.
Article Summary: India had the world's second-highest number of people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, after China, with 444 million Indians affected. India's age- standardised exposure prevalence declined from 43.2% to 30.6% over the last three decades. The study links second- hand smoke to ischaemic heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and breast cancer.

NEW DELHI: Stepping up the fight against malnutrition, which remains a significant health challenge, govt will take the message of dietary diversity and importance of “protein rich foods” in a child’s diet — with special focus on children enrolled in around 14 lakh anganwadi centres — across the country, as part of its annual “Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026”. The month-long nutrition campaign will be launched on Sept 9 from Varanasi.Women and child development (WCD) minister Annpurna Devi said this year’s theme for the campaign “Hamari Anganwadi Hamari Jimmedari” seeks to place anganwadi centres at the heart of community-led action for nutrition and early childhood development.One of the highlights of the Poshan Maah will be the ‘Protein-Rich Foods’ campaign. It is proposed to conduct awareness activities on protein-rich foods from plant and animal sources — pulses, legumes, nuts and seeds, milk and milk products, and eggs — demonstrating practical and affordable ways to add protein to daily diets.In a statement, WCD ministry said the theme seeking to involve community members in each anganwadi will drive the accelerated constitution and operationalisation of anganwadi management committees to promote community oversight of nutrition services, as per guidelines issued in June.This “all-women committee” will have seven members — supervisor associated with the anganwadi as its chairperson, an anganwadi worker as convener, an Asha worker, two mothers of enrolled children, a woman from a self-help group (SHG), NGO or civil society organisation, and a govt school teacher.The ministry highlighted that Supplementary Nutrition Programme (SNP) guidelines for the first time, define hot cooked meals and mandate SNP menu boards in anganwadis. The guidelines also recommend drastically reducing the use of added sugars and salt in supplementary nutrition.
Article Summary: The month-long nutrition campaign will be launched on Sept 9 from Varanasi. The theme for the campaign “Hamari Anganwadi Hamari Jimmedari’ seeks to place anganwadi centres at the heart of community-led action for nutrition.

Article Title: J&K: Suspicious movement prompts search ops in Poonch's frontier villages
Article Text:
Suspicious movement prompts search ops in Poonch’s frontier villages

JAMMU: Security forces launched joint cordon-and-search operations in frontier villages in J&K’s Poonch district on Monday based on inputs about the alleged movement of terror suspects in the area, officials said.“The searches commenced around 12.30pm. Multiple teams are combing the forested upper reaches spanning Jhotian Wali, Dhook Dhoba, and other areas in Mehrote, in Poonch’s Surankote sub-division,” an official said, adding that the operation continued till late Monday.Pertinently, troops of the Army’s 16 RR, 37 RR, and J&K Police’s SOG have been hunting for terror suspects in Surankote since September 2.
Article Summary: Suspicious movement prompts search ops in Poonch’s frontier villages. Multiple teams are combing the forested upper reaches spanning Jhotian Wali, Dhook Dhoba, and other areas in Mehrote, in Surankote sub-division. Troops of the Army and J&K Police have been hunting for terror suspects since September 2.

Article Title: Purification row: Punjab Congress protests Haldwani ritual; demands FIR against organisers
Article Text:
Punjab Congress workers protest against the Haldwani “purification” ritual, demanding action against its organisers

Punjab Congress staged a protest on Monday against the BJP and RSS over a “purification” ritual allegedly conducted at Uttarakhand’s Haldwani Ramlila Ground after a Congress rally attended by party president Mallikarjun Kharge. The protesters also demanded that the FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on the incident be withdrawn.Congress MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa condemned the ritual and demanded action against those who organised it. "The Congress party in Punjab, and across India, does not believe in caste-based discrimination. We demand that an FIR be registered against the person who performed the 'purification' in Haldwani. The false FIR against Rahul Gandhi should be discarded immediately," news agency ANI quoted Randhawa saying.Former Punjab chief minister and Punjab Congress campaign committee chairperson Charanjit Singh Channi said the protest was against what he described as the “discriminatory mindset” of the BJP and RSS. "We have staged a protest against the mindset of the RSS and the BJP, specifically regarding the incident where the stage was 'purified' after Mallikarjun Kharge had stepped onto it.They treated the stage as 'contaminated' simply because a Dalit had set foot on it. An FIR must be registered against those responsible for this act. This protest serves as an expression of our anger and a warning to the government," Channi said.The protest comes days after Haldwani City Kotwali Police registered an FIR against Rahul Gandhi on August 30 following a complaint over his remarks about the ritual. The complainant, Amit Kumar, a 26-year-old Valmiki community member and office-bearer of Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas, alleged that Gandhi's comments hurt the sentiments of the Scheduled Caste community.According to the complaint, Gandhi had on August 29 described the “shuddhikaran yajna” at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground as an act of untouchability and anti-Dalit discrimination. The FIR invokes provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The organisers, however, have denied that the ritual had any caste-based motive.
Article Summary: Congress MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa condemned the ritual and demanded action against those who organised it. The protesters also demanded that the FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on the incident be withdrawn. Gandhi had on August 29 described the “shuddhikaran yajna” at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground as an act of untouchability and anti-Dalit discrimination.

Article Title: ‘Will reduce UP to Orwellian Dystopia’: Allahabad HC raps Noida DM over student’s NSA detention
Article Text:
Akriti Chaudhary, a 24-year-old Delhi University history graduate and student activist, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers’ protest in Noida in April 2026

NEW DELHI: The Allahabad High Court has ordered recovery of Rs 5 lakh from the salaries of the Gautam Buddha Nagar district magistrate and other officials after quashing the National Security Act (NSA) detention of Delhi University student and activist Akriti Chaudhary.The division bench of Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev held that Chaudhary's detention violated her fundamental right to life and personal liberty under Article 21, finding that the material relied upon by authorities did not justify invoking the stringent preventive detention law.The court directed that Rs 5 lakh be paid to Chaudhary as compensation and recovered from the salary of Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Medha Roopam and other officers found responsible, including the SHO who prepared the initial report backing her detention. It also directed that the court's displeasure with the officials be entered in their service records.In a strongly worded September 2 order, the court criticised the manner in which the detention order was passed and warned that continued "despotic" conduct by "errant" bureaucrats could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an "Orwellian Dystopia", reported PTI.Chaudhary, a 24-year-old history graduate, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers' protest in Noida in April 2026.The UP Police invoked the NSA against her and activist-journalist Satya Verma on May 13. They were among activists arrested in cases related to the protest seeking higher wages.The court said the police dossier against Chaudhary contained allegations but lacked credible supporting material. It said the DM was required to independently examine the record before deciding whether preventive detention was warranted."The conduct of the Gautam Buddha Nagar DM who passed the impugned order is worthy of derision," the court said.The bench noted that Chaudhary had no previous criminal record and that there was no material showing she had incited violence. It said the circumstances suggested that the detention was intended to make an example of her and discourage others from exercising their right to freedom of speech and expression in support of labourers.The court also questioned the state's version of when Chaudhary was arrested. It recorded that she was taken into custody around 5.30 pm on April 11 at Botanical Garden Metro Station, although the state claimed her arrest took place on April 12.A notice issued under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was cited by the state. However, the notice carried General Diary Entry No. 37, which was generated only at 10.20 am on April 12."Mentioning the GD number in the notice under section 130 of the BNSS reveals that the petitioner was already arrested and the procedure of giving a notice under section 130 of the BNSS was ex post facto the arrest and nothing more than a sham," Justice Sreedharan said."I agree with the view of brother Justice Achal Sachdev that the notice u/s. 130 of the BNSS was prepared after the arrest of the Petitioner and that is the reason why the time of issuance is not mentioned in the notice and its omission is deliberate," he added.The court said preventive detention under the NSA is an exception and cannot be used in place of ordinary criminal law. It described the grounds of Chaudhary's detention as "repetitive, speculative and are only opinion-based", noting the absence of material supporting those conclusions.It also cautioned authorities against treating peaceful public protests as a threat merely because they could potentially lead to a breach of peace."Preventing people from gathering in public spaces or agitating for their rights on the grounds of assumed breach of peace would be throwing the baby out of the bath water," the court said.The bench said the constitutional protection of freedom of speech and expression extends to peaceful gatherings and collective action, and cannot be curtailed merely on the basis of the state's subjective assessment.The court also reminded bureaucrats and police officers that their duty is to the Constitution rather than the political executive, saying that people are the masters in a democracy.It warned that officials who disregard their constitutional oath could come to be seen as an "oppressive vestige of the British Empire", creating an environment of civil unrest.The court said the judiciary could pass "harsh orders" to compensate citizens where official excesses or illegalities infringe upon civil liberties without adequate cause or due process.
Article Summary: Akriti Chaudhary, a 24-year-old history graduate, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers’ protest in Noida in April 2026. The Allahabad High Court has ordered recovery of Rs 5 lakh from the salaries of the Gautam Buddha Nagar district magistrate and other officials.
